## Strategy guide

**SCPT 289 · Super Argent Flight Guide · 2023-03-08.** Draft synthesis of the complete verified ASR transcript. Compatibility with current rules is unreviewed; speech has no speaker attribution.

### Strategic thesis

Argent’s early strength is cheap reach: two two-move capacity destroyers make early control and a custodians attempt accessible. The guide pairs this with Sarween Tools and Plasma Scoring, then favors Strike Wing Alpha II and PDS II. The advantage can fade, so plan by round three for a stronger fleet and a bonus-point path. The hosts differ on card rankings and how aggressively to pursue alternatives after missing custodians; those disagreements remain conditional.

### Opening and tempo

**C01 — Prefer Sarween Tools and Plasma Scoring as the usual starting technologies; the speakers strongly reject Neural Motivator as a default.** Their default path; a table-specific choice to deny another faction Sarween is acknowledged but not recommended. [Source: 701.60–705.92s (s000191); 801.48–803.98s (s000224); 833.50–840.00s (s000242)]

**C02 — Treat the home system as influence-rich but awkward for early resources and production.** This matters when planning the opening economy and weighing Hololattice against another dock. [Source: 849.94–854.72s (s000246); 887.90–890.06s (s000253); 2390.04–2396.02s (s000633)]

**C03 — Use Zeal’s player-count-scaled early votes as leverage, while recognizing that voting first can be a liability.** Its bonus applies if Argent casts a vote; the hosts are especially negative about three- or four-player games. [Source: 902.92–907.46s (s000258); 910.56–913.22s (s000261); 913.22–917.10s (s000262); 917.28–920.14s (s000263); 928.64–930.88s (s000268); 936.16–937.94s (s000273); 4239.52–4244.68s (s001095); 4266.92–4272.20s (s001103)]

**C04 — Use the starting Strike Wing Alpha I destroyers as cheap two-move capacity units, not as ordinary destroyers.** They can carry a small invasion force, reach custodians, and threaten distant systems alongside the starting carrier. [Source: 1110.46–1113.24s (s000320); 1113.68–1117.62s (s000321); 1117.96–1118.86s (s000322); 1131.64–1136.16s (s000327); 2669.48–2676.36s (s000693)]

**C05 — Exploit Aerie Sentinels’ capacity-free transport to make unexpected or flexible landings.** A capacity ship must be present; the guide says any number of Argent mechs can accompany it without counting against capacity. [Source: 1158.90–1166.62s (s000332); 1171.70–1177.30s (s000334); 1181.82–1189.54s (s000336); 2524.04–2527.42s (s000654)]

### Units and faction abilities

**C06 — Use Trilossa Aun Mirik to spread home-produced ground forces across Argent’s three-planet home system.** Most useful on a large home production; the guide describes the agent as convenient but modest otherwise. [Source: 1330.90–1337.30s (s000361); 1356.80–1361.74s (s000365); 1366.64–1368.10s (s000368); 1389.54–1392.68s (s000377)]

**C07 — Unlock Trrakan Aun Zulok early by building toward six units with AFB, space cannon, or bombardment.** The starting destroyers and home PDS make the unlock accessible; one example is taking Construction secondary and building two destroyers at home. [Source: 1434.48–1437.60s (s000395); 1437.60–1438.96s (s000396); 1439.28–1441.24s (s000397); 1442.94–1444.70s (s000399); 1502.02–1507.62s (s000412); 1513.68–1520.84s (s000415)]

**C08 — Remember that the commander adds a die to one unit-ability roll, including anti-fighter barrage.** The guide names AFB, space cannon, and bombardment; it warns digital tabletop users not to forget to enable the extra die. [Source: 1448.32–1455.60s (s000402); 1462.22–1468.58s (s000405); 1468.58–1473.82s (s000406)]

**C09 — Treat Mirik Aun Sissiri as an opportunistic defensive or repositioning tool, not the foundation of a strategy.** Her action moves ships between tokened systems with no enemy ships; the guide values late defense, with invasion or Malice access as situational cases. [Source: 1524.56–1527.74s (s000417); 1537.08–1542.98s (s000419); 1632.60–1637.52s (s000444); 1643.46–1646.50s (s000447); 1665.28–1668.04s (s000455)]

**C10 — The episode’s FAQ interpretation allows transport out of tokened systems during a movement ability; keep that distinct from a tactical action.** Relevant to the Argent hero and comparable movement abilities. [Source: 1727.46–1729.62s (s000474); 1743.90–1748.62s (s000480); 1757.96–1763.00s (s000486); 1763.34–1766.96s (s000487)]

### Technology and trade

**C11 — Prioritize Strike Wing Alpha II; treat its 9-or-10 infantry effect as extra rather than the main benefit.** A core upgrade for a faction encouraged to build destroyers; infantry aboard ships are the threat described. [Source: 1871.48–1876.42s (s000523); 1899.08–1904.72s (s000528); 1904.72–1909.72s (s000529); 1909.72–1916.28s (s000530); 1962.76–1970.24s (s000540)]

**C12 — Research Aerie Hololattice when production or a home-system fix matters; do not assume its movement restriction secures every slice.** Its Production 1 is attractive at home and on forward planets; the defensive value depends on slice geometry and opponent routes. [Source: 2084.44–2091.54s (s000569); 2107.90–2113.00s (s000573); 2158.72–2163.24s (s000585); 2163.24–2172.58s (s000586); 2281.60–2285.32s (s000606); 2345.42–2349.20s (s000623)]

**C13 — The preferred core technology package is PDS II plus Strike Wing Alpha II.** PDS II deters bullying while Strike Wing II provides efficient midgame fleets; exact timing depends on the board. [Source: 2854.68–2859.18s (s000733); 2868.46–2870.76s (s000737); 2870.76–2873.60s (s000738); 2876.18–2878.76s (s000740)]

**C14 — Consider AI Development Algorithm as an early rebate that bridges core research into a late-game unit upgrade.** One proposed path is PDS II, AI Dev, then Strike Wing II; DET or Antimass may fill prerequisites for Carrier II or Dreadnought II. [Source: 2967.94–2969.28s (s000769); 2969.52–2971.98s (s000770); 2972.38–2976.22s (s000771); 2976.22–2979.28s (s000772); 2979.78–2985.60s (s000774); 3008.04–3013.38s (s000782); 3013.60–3020.68s (s000783)]

**C15 — Choose Carrier II or Dreadnought II according to production and the fleet role needed.** The hosts lean Dread II when production is limited, Carrier II when extra infantry/capacity is needed; Dread II adds bombardment opportunities. [Source: 3024.86–3029.98s (s000785); 3029.98–3037.06s (s000786); 3037.06–3041.04s (s000787); 3044.88–3049.58s (s000789)]

**C16 — Use Dark Energy Tap selectively with Argent’s destroyer-heavy fleet, which can explore and later reposition.** The destroyers remain useful for home defense or late offense, making DET more plausible than for factions using disposable explorers. [Source: 3202.26–3208.00s (s000832); 3213.80–3218.50s (s000834); 3218.92–3223.80s (s000835); 3223.80–3230.76s (s000836)]

**C17 — Reserve Graviton Laser Systems for late-game defense; research earlier only for a visible threat.** The hosts allow earlier Graviton if Argent took custodians, the table has noticed, and Carrier II is not urgent. [Source: 3116.00–3121.68s (s000807); 3141.36–3144.18s (s000812); 3144.72–3147.22s (s000813); 3164.48–3167.68s (s000820); 3167.68–3170.80s (s000821); 3171.36–3173.54s (s000822); 3192.50–3196.74s (s000830)]

**C18 — Use Fleet Logistics to make a planned hero reposition harder to block, not as a token-only feint.** The value is in staging ships, taking a planet, then using the hero to return or defend before opponents can obstruct the destination. [Source: 3254.34–3256.02s (s000843); 3273.06–3276.24s (s000850); 3311.34–3316.58s (s000858); 3316.58–3320.58s (s000859); 3334.22–3336.76s (s000863)]

**C19 — Treat Assault Cannon as an optional red-skip finisher for small ships, not a blind default.** The proposed combination uses AFB and Raid Formation before combat; the speakers recommend it only when a concrete target makes sense. [Source: 3383.50–3387.76s (s000874); 3397.80–3402.74s (s000878); 3407.24–3414.04s (s000880); 3415.62–3423.28s (s000882)]

**C20 — Do not make Integrated Economy or Self-Assembly Routines routine investments; cheap destroyer-plus-mech production already covers much of the role.** A fitting skip or unusual objective can change the choice, but usual tech tempo and available build sites make them hard to justify. [Source: 3488.06–3494.42s (s000903); 3528.12–3536.50s (s000910); 3600.00–3605.40s (s000924); 3616.18–3621.30s (s000927); 3639.24–3643.72s (s000932)]

**C21 — Sell Strike Wing Ambuscade near its ability window; do not overprice vague passive defense, but ask more when it directly enables scoring.** The extra die matters most for a planned offensive/objective roll; Jol-Nar is a stronger buyer because of rerolls. [Source: 3783.48–3786.92s (s000978); 3823.02–3828.02s (s000987); 3856.50–3861.98s (s000994); 3862.38–3865.12s (s000995)]

**C22 — Use the PDS network as a paid deterrent; establish a simple consistent toll and avoid giving space-cannon value away for nothing.** The speakers suggest roughly one trade good normally, with negotiation when the passage or objective is especially important. [Source: 3902.96–3910.04s (s001004); 3910.56–3915.66s (s001005); 3926.94–3932.64s (s001009); 4118.62–4121.18s (s001066)]

**C23 — Keep trade simple and frequent: Argent has three commodities but often reaches more neighbors early than its commodity value suggests.** Several small trades and X-1 opportunities are preferred to one elaborate exchange; Trade can fund flexible spending. [Source: 4132.48–4133.64s (s001072); 4140.60–4145.68s (s001074); 4169.18–4176.24s (s001080); 4916.06–4922.40s (s001265); 4926.24–4931.72s (s001267)]

### Round-one cards and fleet transition

**C24 — Choose round-one cards by whether they enable custodians timing, not a fixed ranking.** Trade, Warfare, or a timed Diplomacy/Technology/Leadership combination may work depending on skips, secondaries, and table choices. [Source: 5048.08–5052.66s (s001302); 5069.80–5077.30s (s001307); 5218.42–5220.58s (s001350); 5354.30–5359.20s (s001393); 5400.00–5404.22s (s001404)]

**C25 — Take Politics when speaker position can preserve round-two custodians or help later speaker control.** Less attractive if round-one custodians is available another way; assess whether the next speaker can score early. [Source: 4708.40–4714.42s (s001213); 4767.78–4774.16s (s001225); 4815.40–4822.12s (s001235)]

**C26 — If custodians is unavailable and Construction is a late pick, place a forward PDS on an important equidistant or in-slice planet.** The hosts favor a forward PDS on valuable slice planets; placement depends on map geometry and neighbors. [Source: 2941.24–2945.18s (s000757); 4829.98–4835.56s (s001237); 4845.30–4850.72s (s001240); 4868.96–4871.10s (s001246)]

**C27 — Do not prioritize Leadership automatically; take it when token pressure or a blue-skip Gravity Drive opening makes its timing valuable.** Home influence often funds one extra token; Leadership is more attractive if it enables round-one Gravity Drive and a later Mecatol grab. [Source: 4501.00–4507.02s (s001152); 4517.52–4521.52s (s001155); 4521.52–4527.98s (s001156); 4527.98–4532.88s (s001157); 4540.90–4543.26s (s001160); 4551.94–4555.62s (s001163)]

**C28 — Start planning the late fleet by round three: Strike Wing IIs can lose when opponents bring more sustained hull points.** Build toward fleet-pool advantage; add carriers, fighters, or dreadnoughts according to objectives, with Hololattice as possible forward production. [Source: 5503.60–5507.82s (s001431); 5513.90–5520.78s (s001433); 5520.78–5528.08s (s001434); 5535.78–5542.00s (s001438); 5576.22–5581.14s (s001448); 5607.38–5611.66s (s001454)]

### Scoring and agenda risks

**C29 — Argent is well positioned for many stage-one control and economic objectives, but early comfort should not obscure custodians’ bonus-point value.** Movement and capacity help with early control; inexpensive fleets and modest tech needs soften stage-one spending objectives. [Source: 5897.48–5901.92s (s001523); 5919.62–5927.34s (s001528); 6000.00–6006.42s (s001550); 6056.12–6060.12s (s001568); 6630.64–6633.94s (s001718)]

**C30 — Expect weaker stage-two economic scoring and prepare an upgraded fleet for major control objectives.** Structure objectives may suit Argent; large resource reserves and taking defended planets can be difficult without ship upgrades. [Source: 6380.60–6385.70s (s001658); 6405.60–6410.48s (s001663); 6445.50–6450.46s (s001678); 6612.58–6617.48s (s001713)]

**C31 — Use bonus AFB rolls to pursue combat secrets such as Turn Their Fleets to Dust and Fight with Precision; treat Occupy the Fringe and Produce en Masse as awkward fits.** Demonstrate Your Power is described as broadly accessible rather than a distinct Argent advantage; printed scoring conditions still apply. [Source: 6109.88–6111.58s (s001584); 6113.26–6119.20s (s001586); 6137.44–6141.88s (s001591); 6141.88–6147.54s (s001592); 6148.08–6151.42s (s001593); 6165.14–6170.26s (s001597); 6170.26–6175.18s (s001598); 6338.16–6342.38s (s001649)]

**C32 — Watch for Representative Government, Articles of War, Rearmament Agreement, and Enforced Travel Ban.** They can remove Zeal’s bonus votes, suppress the mech, or disable PDS near wormholes; allies and agenda control may help. [Source: 5685.00–5688.76s (s001472); 5697.38–5710.30s (s001475); 5743.06–5745.40s (s001485); 5755.24–5759.90s (s001491); 5769.28–5771.98s (s001494); 5839.34–5844.80s (s001510)]

**C33 — After missing custodians, pursue an attainable bonus-point route, but avoid resource-intensive exploration gambles without the means to support them.** One host suggests DET or an accessible Mecatol point route; the other argues Argent lacks Naaz-Rokha’s wealth and repeatable exploration tempo. [Source: 6636.84–6638.62s (s001722); 6676.30–6678.66s (s001734); 6745.88–6750.82s (s001753); 7028.90–7030.66s (s001842)]

**C34 — Use PDS placement and Hololattice to defend valuable routes and production sites, allowing for exposed approaches in an awkward slice.** Structures on tech skips or attachment planets can deter attacks; empty systems and wormhole geometry can undermine coverage. [Source: 2296.18–2299.82s (s000610); 2323.70–2326.60s (s000617); 5464.88–5471.60s (s001422); 5489.34–5492.70s (s001428); 5492.70–5497.40s (s001429)]

**C35 — Do not let early control scores or defense justify delaying the point plan.** Without custodians or another bonus point, Argent may struggle once stage twos arrive; round-three decisions often determine its tempo. [Source: 5404.22–5407.86s (s001405); 5417.04–5421.34s (s001408); 6992.94–6996.28s (s001824); 8391.60–8397.48s (s002216)]

### Component connections

Sarween Tools and Aerie Hololattice form a production pairing (C01, C12; 224, 585–586s). Plasma Scoring and the unlocked commander can make a home PDS roll more threatening (C07–C08; 741–742, 1515s). PDS II and Strike Wing Alpha II cover distinct risks: deterrence and efficient fleet strength (C13; 733–738s). Fleet Logistics can support a hero reposition when the fleet is staged first (C18; 3255–3342s). The Jol-Nar alliance exchange can amplify Argent’s PDS network, but requires a political deal (4347–4381s).

### Edition and ASR limits

Component spellings are normalized against the reference file; transcript variants include “Airy Hollow Lattice” and “Ambuscod.” Raid Formation, hero movement and the Strike Wing II infantry effect are episode interpretations, not current-rules rulings. Agenda advice is date-sensitive. Hosts’ preferences and anecdotes are not verified outcome data.

## Combined source guidance

The guide above contains conditional, transcript-cited advice. The pinned documents below add community research and a bot-oriented mid/late-game profile. Their ordered technology/build lists are proposals, not unconditional policy targets. Keep source disagreements and expansion assumptions visible.

**Historical scope:** upstream statements about available factions, engine support, bot behavior and benchmark results describe that source revision; they are not checks of this checkout. Podcast timestamps in upstream notes are approximate and do not share the local transcript verification.

<details><summary>upstream-community — The Argent Flight (`argent`)</summary>

[Exact pinned section](../sources/upstream-community.md#the-argent-flight-argent) · [Repository source](https://github.com/Feelx234/TI4-Bot-Dev/blob/1fd3092ad83a72bc3e379ac3946852b409adee6d/crates/ti4-server/docs/COMMUNITY_FACTION_STRATEGIES.md#the-argent-flight-argent)

> Historical source excerpt; advice and engine claims retain the source’s assumptions.

**Engine check.** Home Valk 2/0, Ylir 0/2, Avar 1/1 (three planets); start 1 carrier, 2 destroyers,
2 fighters, 5 infantry, PDS, dock; no starting technology in this engine (the printed sheet picks
two; not modelled). Strike Wing Alpha destroyers: move 2, capacity 1, anti-fighter barrage 9 (x2);
Strike Wing Alpha II (RR): combat 7, barrage 6 (x3), 9-10 also kills infantry in space. Raid
Formation: excess barrage hits damage sustain-damage ships. Zeal: vote first, +1 vote per player.
Aerie Hololattice (Y): no movement through systems with your structures; PRODUCTION 1 on planets with
structures. Flagship: no space cannon against your ships in its system. Mech does not use capacity.
Commander (6 units with barrage/space cannon/bombardment): an extra die on unit-ability rolls.

**Opening.** One of the fastest starts: destroyers that carry an infantry each and move 2 reach
equidistant systems in round 1; with the right adjacent system (Arinam/Meer, a red skip) Strike
Wing Alpha II in round 1 and Mecatol Rex in round 2 are possible ([BGG "Argent Flight: the power of
Meer", 2021](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2713427);
[r/ti "Sardakk and Muaat neighbours as Argent", 2023](https://www.reddit.com/r/twilightimperium/comments/14fchyk/how_to_deal_with_sardakk_and_muaat_neighbors_as/)).

**Play.** Stake a claim, hold it with a PDS grid (Aerie Hololattice), then play nice. Strike Wing
Alpha IIs strip fighter screens and damage sustain ships, so cheap destroyers beat expensive fleets
(one guide's estimate: four destroyers worth 4 resources have about a 51% chance against a war sun
with six fighters); Muaat should not fight Argent. Assault Cannon by round 2 is possible. The
three-planet home system is the weak spot, especially against Sardakk's commander (commits from
adjacent systems). Destroyers are excellent for control objectives
([r/ti 2025 tier comments](https://www.reddit.com/r/twilightimperium/comments/1kylhx4/faction_power_tier_list/)).

**Strength.** SCPT row 2 (2022; one commenter "top 3"), async PoK B, but F in SCPT 2025 with 7% async
win rate in Thunder's Edge ("a round-5 faction in round-4 games"). Disagreement is sharp: "a menace
to attack" versus "structure-based without a way to get structures".

**Bot feasibility.**
- Build mix: Strike Wing Alpha destroyers as the main ship (cheap, carry infantry, move 2). In
  `pick_produce` give Argent destroyers carrier-like value for transport. Value high, effort S.
- Opening: activation and movement treat any ship with capacity as a carrier (`capacity() > 0`),
  but the opening plan's transport count (`free_transports_and_ground`) and the opening transport
  bonus in `pick_produce` only count `capacity() >= 2`, so capacity-1 destroyers never count as
  transports there. Count them. Value high, effort S.
- Research: Strike Wing Alpha II first (needs two reds: no starting tech here, so AI Development
  or a red skip), Aerie Hololattice later. Effort S.
- Fight model: anti-fighter barrage and Raid Formation are not in `fleet_strength`; Argent
  under-rates its own destroyers. Value medium, effort M.
- Zeal makes Argent the agenda heavyweight, unused while agendas are random. Effort L.

</details>

## Strategy connections

- [Sarween Tools](../components.md#technology-st) **enables** [Aerie Hololattice](../components.md#technology-ah). Sarween is the normal yellow start; Hololattice Production 1 receives its production discount. Sources: [SCPT 289, 801.48–803.98s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 2158.72–2163.24s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 2163.24–2172.58s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/)
- [Plasma Scoring](../components.md#technology-ps) **synergizes-with** [Trrakan Aun Zulok](../components.md#leader-argentcommander). When both modifiers apply to a qualifying ability roll, the guide describes an especially threatening home PDS roll. Sources: [SCPT 289, 2879.26–2883.16s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 2883.51–2887.92s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 5438.70–5440.66s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/)
- [PDS II](../components.md#technology-pds2) **synergizes-with** [Strike Wing Alpha II](../components.md#technology-swa2). Together they provide the guide’s preferred deterrence and low-cost midgame fleet package; neither guarantees safety. Sources: [SCPT 289, 2854.68–2859.18s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 2868.46–2870.76s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 2870.76–2873.60s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/)
- [Mirik Aun Sissiri](../components.md#leader-argenthero) **enables** [Fleet Logistics](../components.md#technology-fl). Fleet Logistics can stage the fleet before hero movement, reducing the chance an opponent blocks an empty destination. Sources: [SCPT 289, 3254.34–3256.02s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 3273.06–3276.24s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 3311.34–3316.58s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 3316.58–3320.58s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 3334.22–3336.76s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/)
- [Alliance](../components.md#promissory-color-an) **synergizes-with** [PDS II](../components.md#technology-pds2). The guide says the proposed Jol-Nar alliance exchange makes Argent’s PDS network much stronger, while describing it as a political tradeoff. Sources: [SCPT 289, 4347.46–4354.60s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 4354.60–4358.72s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 4372.80–4375.30s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/); [SCPT 289, 4375.30–4378.26s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/)

## Strategy claims

<a id="claim-c01"></a>

- **Draft:** Prefer Sarween Tools and Plasma Scoring as the usual starting technologies; the speakers strongly reject Neural Motivator as a default.
  Conditions: Their default path; a table-specific choice to deny another faction Sarween is acknowledged but not recommended. Compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed. Uncertainty: Strong podcast preference; not universal advice.
  Sources: [SCPT 289 702–706s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 801–804s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 834–840s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/)
  Components: [Sarween Tools](../components.md#technology-st), [Plasma Scoring](../components.md#technology-ps), [Neural Motivator](../components.md#technology-nm)
<a id="claim-c02"></a>

- **Draft:** Treat the home system as influence-rich but awkward for early resources and production.
  Conditions: This matters when planning the opening economy and weighing Hololattice against another dock. Compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed. Uncertainty: Values and strategic impact are guide claims; verify exact planet values against the rules source.
  Sources: [SCPT 289 850–855s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 888–890s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 2390–2396s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/)
  Components: [The Argent Flight](argent.md), [Aerie Hololattice](../components.md#technology-ah)
<a id="claim-c03"></a>

- **Draft:** Use Zeal’s player-count-scaled early votes as leverage, while recognizing that voting first can be a liability.
  Conditions: Its bonus applies if Argent casts a vote; the hosts are especially negative about three- or four-player games. Compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed. Uncertainty: Agenda outcomes depend on table agreements and player count.
  Sources: [SCPT 289 903–907s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 911–913s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 913–917s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 917–920s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 929–931s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 936–938s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 4240–4245s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 4267–4272s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/)
  Components: [Zeal](../components.md#ability-zeal)
<a id="claim-c04"></a>

- **Draft:** Use the starting Strike Wing Alpha I destroyers as cheap two-move capacity units, not as ordinary destroyers.
  Conditions: They can carry a small invasion force, reach custodians, and threaten distant systems alongside the starting carrier. Compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed. Uncertainty: Cheap reach is the point; the guide does not claim late-game durability.
  Sources: [SCPT 289 1110–1113s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 1114–1118s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 1118–1119s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 1132–1136s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 2669–2676s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/)
  Components: [Strike Wing Alpha I](../components.md#unit-argent-destroyer)
<a id="claim-c05"></a>

- **Draft:** Exploit Aerie Sentinels’ capacity-free transport to make unexpected or flexible landings.
  Conditions: A capacity ship must be present; the guide says any number of Argent mechs can accompany it without counting against capacity. Compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed. Uncertainty: Mechanic is summarized from the episode, not separately rules-checked.
  Sources: [SCPT 289 1159–1167s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 1172–1177s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 1182–1190s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 2524–2527s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/)
  Components: [Aerie Sentinel](../components.md#unit-argent-mech), [Strike Wing Alpha I](../components.md#unit-argent-destroyer)
<a id="claim-c06"></a>

- **Draft:** Use Trilossa Aun Mirik to spread home-produced ground forces across Argent’s three-planet home system.
  Conditions: Most useful on a large home production; the guide describes the agent as convenient but modest otherwise. Compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed. Uncertainty: Ability application follows the podcast explanation.
  Sources: [SCPT 289 1331–1337s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 1357–1362s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 1367–1368s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/) · [SCPT 289 1390–1393s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/289-super-argent-flight-guide/)
  Components: [Trilossa Aun Mirik](../components.md#leader-argentagent)
<a id="claim-c07"></a>

- **Draft:** Unlock Trrakan Aun Zulok early by building toward six units with AFB, space cannon, or bombardment.
